Shadow AI: An Existing Liability

Some partners at Howry Breen & Herman already use Claude for drafting and research. That is the right instinct in the wrong configuration. Consumer Claude accounts (individual Pro subscriptions) offer no data isolation, no SOC2 compliance, no zero-retention guarantee, and no audit trail. Under ABA Opinion 512 and Texas Bar Opinion 705, this creates attorney-client privilege exposure today. TRAIGA, in effect since January 1, 2026, classifies Howry Breen & Herman as an AI "deployer" regardless of whether the firm has a formal program. The path forward: migrate to a governed workspace and build on the tools already in use.

The Cost Delta

Ten individual Claude Pro accounts at $20/month each = $2,400/year. Ten Claude Enterprise seats = approximately $3,000–$3,600/year. For roughly $50–$100 per month more, the compliance exposure disappears entirely.

What Changes at the Firm

Rather than asking partners to abandon a tool they use and trust, the first conversation validates their behavior and builds on it. Attorneys who complete Phase 01 workshops arrive at the operations phase with AI fluency already built, which compresses adoption time on every subsequent tool.

Competitive Signal

No Austin PI peer has formal AI governance in place. The first firm to move from informal use to a documented, governed deployment earns a compliance posture that becomes a credible differentiator with referring attorneys and sophisticated clients.

Compliance & Governance

ABA 512 · Texas Bar 705 · TRAIGA · Federal Court Disclosure

6. Compliance & Governance

Howry Breen & Herman is already classified as an AI "deployer" under TRAIGA (Texas Responsible AI Governance Act), in effect since January 1, 2026. Every AI tool the firm uses, including the informal consumer Claude accounts partners currently have, falls within scope. The governance program described here produces a complete compliance infrastructure: a record defensible in a State Bar inquiry or malpractice proceeding, built to survive scrutiny.

Regulatory Landscape
ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 2024)

Six ethics obligations: competence, confidentiality, communication, candor to tribunal, supervision, and billing. Written firm AI policy required. Immediate professional standard.

Texas Bar Opinion 705 (Feb 2025)

Independent verification of AI outputs before filing or advising. AI efficiency gains must benefit hourly clients. Human oversight mandatory at all stages.

TRAIGA HB 149 (In effect Jan 1, 2026)

Law firms using AI for intake, research, drafting, or marketing are "deployers." Enforcement by Texas AG. Notice-to-cure process; civil penalties for uncured violations.

Federal Court AI Disclosure

Northern District of Texas: attorney certification required that AI-drafted language has been independently verified. Standing orders accelerating across all federal courts.

What the Full Governance Program Covers

Eight deliverables that together constitute a defensible compliance record. Built in Phase 02 (Presence):

1.Written AI Use Policy addressing all 6 ABA Opinion 512 ethics obligations
2.Texas Bar Opinion 705 human oversight protocols and hallucination risk documentation
3.TRAIGA deployer obligations package for every AI tool in the firm's stack
4.Federal and state court AI disclosure matrix for every court where the firm practices
5.Vendor/tool assessment framework applied to every tool in the stack at go-live
6.Client disclosure templates for matters where AI materially affects representation
7.Billing policy for AI-assisted work under Texas Bar Opinion 705
8.Attorney and paralegal training sessions on the full compliance framework
Phase 01 (Protect) builds the initial governance layer. Phase 02 (Presence) completes the full program. Sequential and non-duplicative.

AEO + GEO Strategy

Answer Engine & Generative Engine Optimization for AI-Native Search

7. AEO + GEO Strategy

AI platforms now generate 45 billion sessions per month. ChatGPT holds 64–68% of the AI chatbot market. Google AI Overviews appear in 57% of long-tail legal queries. AI-driven traffic grew 257% year-over-year. The search landscape has structurally changed: the firm that earns AI citations earns the prospect before they see a single blue link. Fewer than 5% of Austin PI firms have any formal AEO strategy. The compounding window is open now.

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)

AEO structures the firm's content so AI crawlers extract and cite it directly in generated answers. Six structural changes required:

01
Attorney Schema Markup on every profile: name, bar number, practice areas, location, awards, and case results in JSON-LD format.
02
FAQ Architecture: 50 pages answering Texas PI questions with direct, AI-extractable answers in the first 50 words.
03
Expanded Results Page: Per-case detail (injury type, jurisdiction, resolution method, timeline) that AI systems cite as specific, verifiable authority.
04
Directory Normalization: 40+ legal directories (Avvo, Justia, FindLaw, Google Business) with consistent NAP data that AI cross-references before citing any firm.
05
Content Freshness Signals: Regular updates to the Results page and case summaries keep the firm's citation profile active. AI systems weight recently updated, authoritative pages higher than static ones.
06
Internal Linking Architecture: Cross-linking FAQ pages, verdict pages, and attorney profiles creates a content network AI crawlers traverse. Isolated pages rarely earn citations; connected ones compound.
Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)

GEO ensures AI platforms cite the firm by name when a user asks for an Austin PI attorney recommendation. Three priorities:

Earned Media Citations
Pitch major verdicts to Texas Lawyer, Law360, and Austin Business Journal. AI systems weight third-party press coverage as a primary authority citation source. Earned media creates the citation trail Wikipedia cannot reliably provide.
Press Citation Building
Every verdict or settlement above $1M pitched to Texas Lawyer, Law360, and local news. AI systems crawl and weight press mentions as authority signals.
Consistent NAP Data
Name, address, phone consistent across all 40+ legal directories. Every AI system querying for Austin PI firms retrieves identical, authoritative information about the firm.
Howry Breen & Herman's Raw Material Advantage
The $53.9M verdict, $34.8M settlement, and $50M settlement are exactly the kind of specific, verifiable, high-authority data points AI systems cite. Properly structured, these make the firm one of the strongest AEO candidates in the Austin market.
AEO/GEO Compounding Returns (Phase 02 Presence)

5–10 AI citations established. 3–5 monthly organic PI leads from AI search. Revenue impact: $300K–$750K.

Firms implementing AEO today are generating 3.4x more AI search traffic than competitors who have not started. AI systems learn from historical citation patterns: a firm cited consistently for 12 months becomes the default source for that jurisdiction and practice area. Latecomers cannot buy their way into that position.

An Approach by Phases

Protect · Presence · Propel

8. An Approach by Phases

Before outlining the approach, it helps to understand what the market looks like without one. A full legal AI stack (practice management, intake CRM, demand letter AI, medical record review, legal research, AEO infrastructure, and compliance documentation) carries a combined annual license cost of $81,000 to $100,000 per year if purchased off-the-shelf. That number does not include implementation, configuration, training, or the workflow integration work that determines whether the tools get used.

Firms that attempt this without a structured implementation partner typically see 60% of tools underutilized within six months, Shadow AI exposure persisting in parallel, and no measurable improvement in intake conversion or case efficiency. Firms that go to Big 4 consultancies for managed implementation pay $500,000 or more over 12 to 18 months, with junior staff executing at senior billing rates and a timeline that keeps the firm exposed while the engagement runs its course.

Neither path is the right fit for a 10-attorney firm with specific operational gaps and a defined competitive window. The approach here is structured differently: three phases, each with a single mandate, each designed to validate before the next one is funded. The firm starts with Phase 01, which closes the liability that already exists. Phase 02 builds the long-term acquisition presence the firm's verdict record makes possible. Phase 03 is the operational infrastructure build, scoped to the firm's actual workflows and investment appetite once Phase 01 has demonstrated what the foundation can support. Full details on pricing and scope are in Section 9.

Advisory Retainer

Ongoing Engagement · Four Service Areas · Three Tiers

10. Advisory Retainer

The three phases deliver infrastructure. What sustains it is an ongoing working relationship. AI tools evolve, regulations shift, staff turns over, and new case types create new workflow demands. The Advisory Retainer keeps Archificials engaged as the firm's dedicated AI advisor after implementation: monitoring performance, handling configuration changes, onboarding new staff, and staying ahead of compliance requirements so the firm does not have to.

01   Compliance Monitoring

The regulatory landscape governing AI in legal practice is still forming. ABA guidance, Texas Bar opinions, and TRAIGA implementation rules will evolve. Archificials tracks those developments, updates the firm's Governance Charter accordingly, and flags any required changes to tool configuration or workflow protocols before they become a disciplinary exposure.

02   Staff Onboarding & Training

Associate turnover at PI firms is real. Every new attorney or paralegal who joins without structured AI onboarding reverts to ad-hoc consumer tool usage, recreating the exact Shadow AI exposure Phase 01 closed. Retainer hours cover onboarding sessions for new hires, refresher training as tools are updated, and dedicated coaching for staff who need more support.

03   Custom Case Configuration

Complex litigation does not fit a template. A new MDL, a mass tort with unique documentation requirements, or a high-value wrongful death case may require custom Claude configurations, new prompt workflows, or adjusted Human-in-the-Loop protocols. Archificials builds those configurations on demand, specific to the matter and the attorneys handling it.

04   Performance Reviews & Optimization

Quarterly reviews covering intake conversion metrics, AI search citation tracking, tool utilization rates, and workflow efficiency benchmarks. Archificials identifies what is working, what is underperforming, and where the next improvement is. Each review produces a prioritized action list for the following quarter, keeping the firm's AI investment compounding rather than plateauing.
